full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs instituted the suit for ejectment of the defendant alleging that the defendant was a tenant under them and he paid rent of the suit property upto 1379 BS and from 1380 BS he stopped payment and as such he is a defaulter in payment of rent of the suit property. The defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement contending that in 1960 he paid Tk. 500.00 to one Julfu Miah and from him he took over possession of the suit property and thereafter he had made construction over there and his homoeopathy dispensary as well as residential house are situated in the suit property. It is further stated that his name was mutated in the municipality as well as in the office of the Electricity Department. It is further stated that he took possession of the suit property with an assurance that he will subsequently purchase the suit property from the plaintiffs, but he is not a tenant of the suit property and he never paid any monthly rent to the land-lord of the suit premises. Both the parties adduced evidence both oral and documentary and after considering the material evidence on record, the learned Judge found that the defendant was a defaulter of the premises and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the defendant-petitioner preferred this Revisional application before this Court. 

 3. Mr. Faruque Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that since the defendant claimed right and title over the suit premises, the present SCC suit is not maintainable. The learned SCC Judge has considered this aspect in detail. It appears that the plaintiffs produced a number of documents with regard to their title and possession of the suit property which have been marked as exhibits. The defendant simply stated that one of the plaintiffs named Julfu Miah took Tk. 500.00 and handed over possession to the defendant But he could not prove as to how and why this possession was made over after taking Tk. 500.00. The defendant could not produce any evidence in support of his stand that he had some sort of right and title over the suit property; rather prima facie it appears that the plaintiffs are the owners and possessors of the property in question. Only the verbal assertion that the defendant paid Tk. 500.00 and he got possession of the suit land will not create any right and title over the property and as such the contention of Mr. Faruque is of no substance. 

 4. Mr. Bazlur Rahman Talukdar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-parties, submits that the defendant failed to establish that there was no relationship between them as landlord and tenant and as such this decree is illegal and void. In order to prove the tenancy the plaintiffs examined 5 witnesses. Their evidence were considered by the trial Court which found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove the case that the defendant was their tenant. In this connection Mr. BR Talukdar has referred to Ext. 4 which is the statement of the defendant-petitioner before the union parishad when a dispute was referred to the union parishad and the members of the union parishad and others had effected a settlement. This Ext. 4 clearly shows that the defendant admitted himself as tenant there and there was dispute between the defendant and the plaintiffs. Mr. BR Talukdar submits that in his deposition the defendant denied his statement made in Ext. 4. But it was proved by a member of the union parishad who was present there that he himself admitted in his statement made before the union parishad about his tenancy. There is no reason to disbelieve this written statement, Ext. 4. Considering the evidence of PWs 1 to 4 together with this Ext. 4 it is clearly proved that the defendant was inducted there as tenant and there was dispute between the parties with regard to payment of rent. 

 5. Further, two certified copies of the decrees of money suits have been filed. From the aforesaid decrees it appears that the plaintiffs filed money suit for realization of the arrear rent and the plaintiffs got a decree. The defendant preferred appeal. But, ultimately, the appeal was dismissed and decree was maintained. So, from this it appears that the plaintiffs are the landlord and the defendant was a tenant under them. It was found by the Court that in that money suit a decree was passed in favour of the plaintiffs. So, from the materials on record I am of the view that the plaintiffs have been able to establish the relationship with the defendant as landlord and tenant and the defendant paid rent upto 1379 BS and thereafter failed to pay rent and he is now illegally claiming right and title over the suit property which was not even accepted by the Court in its decree passed in the previous money suit. 

 6. Mr. Faruque Ahmed lastly submits that the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was not legally issued by the plaintiffs inasmuch as the notice was not duly signed by all the plaintiffs. Mr. BR Talukdar, the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties, has referred to Ext. 7 which is the letter of authority given by all other plaintiffs to plaintiff Serajul Islam in order to deal with the suit property. The notice was issued by the plaintiff Serajul Islam who signed it on behalf of other plaintiffs. So, if the notice is considered along with Ext.7, it appears that the notice was legally issued by the plaintiffs as required under law and there is no lacuna in issuance and service of the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. The contention of Mr. Faruque Ahmed on this point has no substance. 

 7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and ate material evidence on record, it appears to me that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their case and the trial Court has considered the documents and evidence legally and passed a decree in favour of the plaintiffs. I do not find that the learned trial Court has committed any error of law in its decision occasioning failure of justice and as such it is not required by this Court to interfere with the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
